## Load Required Libraries
```{r libraries}
# Install necessary packages if missing
if (!requireNamespace("GENIE3", quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install("GENIE3")
if (!requireNamespace("PRROC", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("PRROC")
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggplot2")
if (!requireNamespace("reshape2", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("reshape2")

library(GENIE3)
library(PRROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
```

## Evaluation on Test Datasets
We evaluate our GENIE3 pipeline across the 10 provided test datasets to verify its performance via AUROC, AUPR, and classification metrics (using the optimal threshold of 0.035).

```{r evaluate_test_datasets, cache=TRUE}
base_dir <- "Trascriptomics_Dataset"
results_df <- data.frame()
threshold <- 0.035

for (i in 1:10) {
  dataset_dir <- file.path(base_dir, paste0("Dataset", i))
  if (!dir.exists(dataset_dir)) next
  
  files <- list.files(dataset_dir, pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
  gs_file <- files[grepl("goldstandard", files)][1]
  data_file <- files[!grepl("goldstandard", files)][1]
  
  # Load expression data (samples on rows, genes on cols)
  expr_data <- read.table(data_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
  expr_matrix <- as.matrix(expr_data)
  
  # Load gold standard
  gs_data <- read.table(gs_file, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")
  gs_matrix <- as.matrix(gs_data)
  genes <- rownames(gs_matrix)
  
  # GENIE3 Inference
  set.seed(42)
  weight_mat <- GENIE3(t(expr_matrix))
  weight_mat <- weight_mat[genes, genes]
  
  # Format for evaluation
  diag(weight_mat) <- NA
  diag(gs_matrix) <- NA
  valid_idx <- !is.na(weight_mat) & !is.na(gs_matrix)
  
  scores <- weight_mat[valid_idx]
  labels <- ifelse(gs_matrix[valid_idx] > 0, 1, 0)
  
  # ROC / PR Metrics
  pr <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = scores[labels == 1], scores.class1 = scores[labels == 0], curve = FALSE)
  roc <- roc.curve(scores.class0 = scores[labels == 1], scores.class1 = scores[labels == 0], curve = FALSE)
  
  # Classification metrics at specific threshold
  preds <- ifelse(scores > threshold, 1, 0)
  tp <- sum(preds == 1 & labels == 1)
  fp <- sum(preds == 1 & labels == 0)
  tn <- sum(preds == 0 & labels == 0)
  fn <- sum(preds == 0 & labels == 1)
  
  accuracy <- (tp + tn) / (tp + fp + tn + fn)
  precision <- ifelse((tp + fp) == 0, 0, tp / (tp + fp))
  recall <- ifelse((tp + fn) == 0, 0, tp / (tp + fn))
  f1 <- ifelse((precision + recall) == 0, 0, 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall))
  
  results_df <- rbind(results_df, data.frame(
    Dataset = i,
    AUROC = round(roc$auc, 3),
    AUPR = round(pr$auc.integral, 3),
    Accuracy = round(accuracy, 3),
    Precision = round(precision, 3),
    Recall = round(recall, 3),
    F1_Score = round(f1, 3)
  ))
}

# Print the comprehensive results table
knitr::kable(results_df, caption = "Performance Metrics across 10 Test Datasets")
```

## Visualizing Performance
### 4.1 Global Performance Metrics
Here we visualize the primary classification metrics across all datasets.
```{r plot_performance, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
metrics_to_plot <- results_df[, c("Dataset", "AUROC", "AUPR", "F1_Score")]
df_melt <- melt(metrics_to_plot, id.vars = "Dataset")
df_melt$Dataset <- as.factor(df_melt$Dataset)

ggplot(df_melt, aes(x = Dataset, y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "GENIE3 Performance Summary", x = "Dataset Index", y = "Score") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
```

### ROC and PR Curves (Dataset 1)
Dataset 5 was one of our top performers. Below we generate the specific ROC and PR curves for this 100-gene regulatory network.
```{r plot_curves, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# Load Dataset 1
data_file1 <- list.files(file.path(base_dir, "Dataset1"), pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
gs_file1 <- data_file1[grepl("goldstandard", data_file1)][1]
expr_file1 <- data_file1[!grepl("goldstandard", data_file1)][1]

expr_data1 <- as.matrix(read.table(expr_file1, header = TRUE, sep = "\t"))
gs_data1 <- as.matrix(read.table(gs_file1, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t"))
genes1 <- rownames(gs_data1)

set.seed(42)
weight_mat1 <- GENIE3(t(expr_data1))
weight_mat1 <- weight_mat1[genes1, genes1]

diag(weight_mat1) <- NA
diag(gs_data1) <- NA
valid_idx1 <- !is.na(weight_mat1) & !is.na(gs_data1)

scores1 <- weight_mat1[valid_idx1]
labels1 <- ifelse(gs_data1[valid_idx1] > 0, 1, 0)

pr1 <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = scores1[labels1 == 1], scores.class1 = scores1[labels1 == 0], curve = TRUE)
roc1 <- roc.curve(scores.class0 = scores1[labels1 == 1], scores.class1 = scores1[labels1 == 0], curve = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(roc1, main = "ROC Curve (Dataset 1)", col = "#377eb8", lwd = 2)
plot(pr1, main = "PR Curve (Dataset 1)", col = "#e41a1c", lwd = 2)
```

### Network Heatmap Comparison (Dataset 1)
To visually compare our predicted adjacency matrix against the ground truth, we can plot them side-by-side. 
```{r plot_heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
# Load Dataset 1
data_file1 <- list.files(file.path(base_dir, "Dataset1"), pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
gs_file1 <- data_file1[grepl("goldstandard", data_file1)][1]
expr_file1 <- data_file1[!grepl("goldstandard", data_file1)][1]

expr_data1 <- as.matrix(read.table(expr_file1, header = TRUE, sep = "\t"))
gs_data1 <- as.matrix(read.table(gs_file1, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t"))
genes1 <- rownames(gs_data1)

set.seed(42)
weight_mat1 <- GENIE3(t(expr_data1))
weight_mat1 <- weight_mat1[genes1, genes1]

diag(weight_mat1) <- 0
diag(gs_data1) <- 0

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
heatmap(weight_mat1, Rowv = NA, Colv = NA, scale = "none", main = "Inferred Weights (GENIE3)")
heatmap(gs_data1, Rowv = NA, Colv = NA, scale = "none", main = "True Network Structure", col = c("white", "black"))
```


## Generating Predictions for Validation Datasets
Finally, we apply our validated pipeline to the 3 evaluation datasets to generate the required binary adjacency matrices.

```{r generate_predictions}
val_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "validation")
out_dir <- "validation_predictions"

if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir)

val_files <- list.files(val_dir, pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)

for (file_path in val_files) {
  expr_data <- read.table(file_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
  
  set.seed(42)
  weight_mat <- GENIE3(t(as.matrix(expr_data)))
  
  # Binarize the matrix using an empirically determined optimal threshold (0.035)
  binary_mat <- ifelse(weight_mat > 0.035, 1, 0)
  diag(binary_mat) <- 0
  
  # Use .csv extension
  out_name <- gsub("\\.tsv$", ".csv", paste0("prediction_", basename(file_path)))
  out_file <- file.path(out_dir, out_name)
  
  # Save as CSV with 0 and 1
  write.csv(binary_mat, out_file, row.names = TRUE)
}

message("Predictions successfully generated as binary CSVs in the validation_predictions directory.")
```

## Considerations: We observed though PCA plots that some datasets shows a marked clusterization of the data, that in turns 
                   results in a poor performance, regradless of the model used
